meta.title: OpenEmux — A simple way to play your retro collection</title>
meta.description: content="OpenEmux is a free and open-source emulation frontend that uses RetroArch underneath. It makes RetroArch easier for anyone who just wants to play: add your own games, pick one, and it starts. Linux is its main platform; Windows is supported too, in beta." />

features.shelf:
Your games, by console

The games you add are grouped by console, with cover art downloaded from the libretro thumbnail archive.
features.first_boot:
Ready on first launch

The first time it opens, OpenEmux creates its configuration and downloads the cores your consoles need, usually in about ten seconds. The rest keep downloading in the background.
features.controls:
Controls per console

Set keyboard and gamepad buttons for each console in one panel. OpenEmux passes them to RetroArch when a game starts.
features.shaders:
Shaders per console

Choose a CRT or scanline shader for each console from a short list, without going through RetroArch's shader menu.
features.native:
Linux first

Linux is OpenEmux's main platform. The app is built with GTK4 and Adwaita, follows the GNOME guidelines, and every change is tested on Linux first. Windows is supported too, with a build still in beta.
features.bios:
BIOS checklist

Shows which BIOS files each console needs and which ones you already have, so a missing file does not end up as a game that silently fails to start.
philosophy.title: Play the games you own
philosophy.lede: OpenEmux is a frontend for RetroArch, made so that someone who just wants to play does not have to learn RetroArch's menus first. It is not a source of games: it ships no games, no ROMs and no BIOS files, and never will.
philosophy.own: • Use only content you legally own. Dump your own cartridges and discs, or use backups of games you purchased.
philosophy.piracy: • Piracy isn't what this is for. Downloading copyrighted games you don't own is illegal in most countries.
philosophy.history: • Emulation helps preserve history. A lot of gaming's art, music and design lives on aging hardware. Keeping it playable is worthwhile, and it works best when it respects the people who made these games.
more.title: Everything else
more.retroarch:
Built on RetroArch

Under the hood, the emulation is done by RetroArch. It is powerful, but its menus and settings can be a lot for someone who just wants to play. OpenEmux takes care of what is around it: organizing your games, downloading the cores, and setting up controls and shaders.
systems.lede: Each system runs on RetroArch's own cores, and has its own cover art, controls and shader settings in OpenEmux.
shots.title: Every console, as cartridges.
shots.lede: Each console has a page with its games on their own cartridges. Switch to covers or a list when you like.
install.title: Installing
install.lede: There are packages for Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora, an AppImage, a Flatpak, an installer for Windows and an APK for Android. On first launch OpenEmux sets up the rest.
install.flatpak_note: Updates arrive with flatpak update. A single-file .flatpak bundle is on the Releases page too.
install.windows_lede: Both builds carry GTK 4, the Python runtime and RetroArch itself, so there is nothing to install alongside them. Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. It is new — if something misbehaves, open an issue.
install.installer_note: Installs for your user only, so no administrator prompt. The builds are not code-signed yet: SmartScreen will warn, and More info → Run anyway gets past it.
install.portable_note: Unzip it anywhere and run OpenEmux.exe from the OpenEmux\ folder inside. Good for a USB stick or a machine you cannot install software on.
install.verify_lede: Every release ships a SHA256SUMS file. Put it next to the artifact you downloaded and run:
install.verify_ok: OK means the file is exactly what was published. Anything else means it is corrupt or tampered with — don't run it.
install.verify_windows: On Windows, PowerShell prints the hash and you compare it by eye with the matching line in SHA256SUMS:
install.build: Prefer building it yourself? make bootstrap && make run — see the build instructions.
thanks.title: Inspired by OpenEmu, powered by RetroArch
thanks.lede: OpenEmux is inspired by OpenEmu, the emulator frontend for macOS. OpenEmu only runs on macOS, so OpenEmux tries to offer something similar on Linux, and now on Windows too. It is not a fork and shares no code with OpenEmu: it is a separate codebase in Python, GTK 4 and libadwaita, and the emulation itself comes from the RetroArch and libretro projects. The console icons are OpenEmu's artwork, credited under OpenEmu's BSD license. The Android app is an independent design (there is no OpenEmu for phones). OpenEmux is not affiliated with or endorsed by the OpenEmu Team. None of this would exist without the work of all these projects. ❤️
support.title: OpenEmux is free software
support.lede: It is free to use, and the code is open under the MIT license. If you would like to help, bug reports, translations, code and ideas are always welcome. On r/OpenEmux you can ask for help, share your setup or follow what is being worked on.
footer.made: Made with lots of love and care by Guilherme Feitoza 🇧🇷
footer.disclaimer: OpenEmux is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or associated with OpenEmu, RetroArch, libretro, Nintendo, Sega, Sony, Atari, or any other company. All trademarks are the property of their respective owners. OpenEmux distributes no games, ROMs, or BIOS files.

android.title: A controller for each console.
android.lede: On Android, every console has its own on-screen controller, in portrait and in landscape. Connect a gamepad and it steps aside.
share.title: From one device to another.
share.lede: On the same Wi-Fi, send a game from your computer to your phone, or back. No account, no cloud, no cable.
share.cap1:
Pick a game on your phone.

Your computer shows up in the list by itself.
share.cap2:
The same code shows on both screens.

If they match, accept on the computer.
share.cap3:
The game goes straight over your Wi-Fi.

Nothing leaves your home network.
share.cap4:
It is in your library now.

Open it and play on the big screen.

android.skins:
A skin for every console

Each of the 31 consoles has its own on-screen controller, laid out like the original pad, in portrait and in landscape. A strip under the picture saves, loads, turns on turbo and speeds the game up.
android.carts:
Cartridges and covers

Games show up as cartridges with their labels, or as covers and a list. The shelves can be put in any order.
android.setup:
Ready after one download

The app does not carry the cores: the first time it opens, it downloads the ones every console needs from the RetroArch buildbot, with the system files PSP and GameCube use.
android.gamepad:
Gamepad too

Connect a controller and the on-screen skin steps aside: the game takes the whole screen, and the menus follow the D-pad and buttons.
android.themes:
Light and dark

Follows the phone's theme, or pick one in Settings.
android.languages:
Eight languages

The same languages as the desktop app, following the phone or chosen in Settings.
android.achievements:
RetroAchievements

Sign in once in Settings and every game unlocks achievements on your RetroAchievements profile, with hardcore mode when you want it.
android.source: Android 8 or newer, 64-bit (arm64). The Android app is a fork of RetroArch, so it is licensed under the GPLv3; its source is at openemux-android.
install.android_lede: The APK is not on the Play Store yet: download it from Releases and allow your browser or file manager to install apps when Android asks. Android 8 or newer, 64-bit.
install.android_note: Open the downloaded file and confirm. Updates are installed the same way, over the previous version.
install.android_first_note: The first time it opens, the app downloads the emulator cores. Then put your ROMs in Import, or in Android/data/com.openemux.mobile/files/roms on the phone.
